glossary.definition: The role accountable for decisions and review of a defined process.
An agreed statement of where mapped work starts and ends, naming the triggering event, the output, and the recipient, without implying that work outside the boundary is unimportant.
The point at which one role transfers an output to the next role, complete only when the receiving role has the information needed to act.

recordNames: Completed process map with boundary record
Vendor statement or demonstrated behavior record
Review record noting date, evidence examined, disagreements, and resolution owners

decisions: Agree on the mapping purpose before selecting symbols or opening a drawing tool
Determine which workflow to examine and record that choice with the map
Resolve disagreement on mapping purpose before treating the map as a basis for a software decision
Decide whether a site difference belongs on a common map, in a linked local instruction, or in a separate process
Record whether each vendor behavior was shown, described, or left unanswered
Assign a resolution owner for any unresolved exception or boundary
Decide who can view, propose, review, and release a change to a process map

decisions: Name the decision the quality and operations team must make before beginning evaluation
Agree on what the team will test and who will judge the result
Separate requirements from preferences in the evaluation record
Agree on observable outcomes before the demonstration session
Record what was not demonstrated and assign follow-up responsibility
Decide whether a gap is a reason to reject an option or requires another session or agreed temporary procedure
Decide whether available evidence supports a selection or whether further information is required
Keep commercial and operational decisions separate in the record
Determine cause before assigning a cause to an unavailable linked item
